text:
ConocoPhillips rose 2.6% today as oil prices surged on geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and Eastern Europe. Brent crude climbed above $106 per barrel following a deadly Saudi airport attack, while ongoing uncertainty around the Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire and potential U.S. military involvement against Iran-backed Houthis threatened global oil supply. For an oil producer like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices directly translate to stronger profits and cash flow.

The stock's 9% gain over two weeks reflects a broader shift in energy markets—crude has moved sharply higher amid these regional conflicts, and investors are betting that geopolitical risk will keep prices elevated. The wide gap between U.S. oil ($96/barrel) and world prices ($125/barrel) also signals tight global supply and premium valuations for producers with international exposure.
